Marathon Petroleum's stock fell 0.2% today, capping a sharper 1.5% decline over two weeks as crude oil prices have dropped from $414.64 on November 13 to $367.19 today. The underlying driver is the retreat in U.S. oil prices to $89.53 per barrel — refiners' profit margins depend directly on the spread between crude input costs and refined product prices, so lower crude prices reduce that spread and compress refinery earnings. Refineries are running at high capacity (95.7%), but that activity only benefits a refiner if the margin is wide enough to cover costs and generate profit.

Geopolitical risk in the Middle East — fresh drone and projectile attacks between Iran-backed forces and Saudi Arabia — has not been enough to push prices higher or sustain the two-week selloff, suggesting markets may be pricing in either supply assurances or a belief that tensions won't escalate into broader disruptions. The permitting reform bill that passed the Senate this week should help energy projects long-term, but it doesn't address the immediate headwind of lower crude valuations bearing down on refinery margins right now.
